[495](https://docs.rs#495)
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// Describes a file system event
[497](https://docs.rs#497)///
[498](https://docs.rs#498)/// From [inotify(7)]:
[499](https://docs.rs#499)///
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// > To determine what events have occurred, an application [read(2)]s
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// > from the inotify file descriptor.  If no events have so far occurred,
[502](https://docs.rs#502)/// > then, assuming a blocking file descriptor, [read(2)] will block until
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// > at least one event occurs (unless interrupted by a signal, in which
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// > case the call fails with the error EINTR; see [signal(7)]).
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// >
[506](https://docs.rs#506)/// > Each successful [read(2)] returns a buffer containing one or more of
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// > this structure.
[508](https://docs.rs#508)///
[509](https://docs.rs#509)/// [inotify(7)]: http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html
[510](https://docs.rs#510)/// [read(2)]: http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/read.2.html
[511](https://docs.rs#511)/// [signal(7)]: http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal.7.html
[512](https://docs.rs#512)#[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
[513](https://docs.rs#513)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[514](https://docs.rs#514)#[repr(C)]
[515](https://docs.rs#515)pub struct inotify_event {
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    /// Identifies the watch for which this event occurs
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    ///
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    /// This is one of the watch descriptors returned by a previous call to
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    /// [`inotify_add_watch()`].
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    ///
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    /// [`inotify_add_watch()`]: fn.inotify_add_watch.html
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    pub wd: c_int,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    /// Describes the type file system event
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    ///
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    /// One of the following bits will be set, to identify the type of event:
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    ///
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    /// - [`IN_ACCESS`]
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    /// - [`IN_ATTRIB`]
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// - [`IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`]
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    /// - [`IN_CLOSE_WRITE`]
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// - [`IN_CREATE`]
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    /// - [`IN_DELETE`]
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// - [`IN_DELETE_SELF`]
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    /// - [`IN_IGNORED`]
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    /// - [`IN_MODIFY`]
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    /// - [`IN_MOVED_FROM`]
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// - [`IN_MOVED_TO`]
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    /// - [`IN_MOVE_SELF`]
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// - [`IN_OPEN`]
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// - [`IN_Q_OVERFLOW`]
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    /// - [`IN_UNMOUNT`]
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    ///
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    /// Some constants cover multiple bits, and can be used for a less precise
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    /// check of the event type:
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    ///
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    /// - [`IN_CLOSE`]
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    /// - [`IN_MOVE`]
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    ///
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    /// In addition, the [`IN_ISDIR`] bit can be set.
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    ///
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    /// [`IN_ACCESS`]: constant.IN_ACCESS.html
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// [`IN_ATTRIB`]: constant.IN_ATTRIB.html
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    /// [`IN_CLOSE`]: constant.IN_CLOSE.html
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    /// [`IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`]: constant.IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE.html
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    /// [`IN_CLOSE_WRITE`]: constant.IN_CLOSE_WRITE.html
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// [`IN_CREATE`]: constant.IN_CREATE.html
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    /// [`IN_DELETE`]: constant.IN_DELETE.html
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// [`IN_DELETE_SELF`]: constant.IN_DELETE_SELF.html
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    /// [`IN_IGNORED`]: constant.IN_IGNORED.html
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// [`IN_ISDIR`]: constant.IN_ISDIR.html
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    /// [`IN_MODIFY`]: constant.IN_MODIFY.html
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    /// [`IN_MOVE`]: constant.IN_MOVE.html
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// [`IN_MOVED_FROM`]: constant.IN_MOVED_FROM.html
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// [`IN_MOVED_TO`]: constant.IN_MOVED_TO.html
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// [`IN_MOVE_SELF`]: constant.IN_MOVE_SELF.html
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    /// [`IN_OPEN`]: constant.IN_OPEN.html
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// [`IN_Q_OVERFLOW`]: constant.IN_Q_OVERFLOW.html
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// [`IN_UNMOUNT`]: constant.IN_UNMOUNT.html
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    pub mask: u32,
[571](https://docs.rs#571)
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    /// A number that connects related events
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    ///
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    /// Currently used only for rename events. A related pair of
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    /// [`IN_MOVED_FROM`] and [`IN_MOVED_TO`] events will have the same,
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    /// non-zero, cookie. For all other events, cookie is 0.
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    ///
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    /// [`IN_MOVED_FROM`]: constant.IN_MOVED_FROM.html
[579](https://docs.rs#579)    /// [`IN_MOVED_TO`]: constant.IN_MOVED_TO.html
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    pub cookie: u32,
[581](https://docs.rs#581)
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    /// The length of `name`
[583](https://docs.rs#583)    ///
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Used to determine the size of this structure. When `name`
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    /// isn't present (`name` is only present when an event occurs
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// for a file inside a watched directory), it is 0. When `name`
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// *is* present, it counts all of `name`'s bytes, including `\0`.
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    ///
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// > The `name` field is present only when an event is returned for
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// > a file inside a watched directory; it identifies the file
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    /// > pathname relative to the watched directory. This pathname is
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// > null-terminated, and may include further null bytes ('\0') to
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// > align subsequent reads to a suitable address boundary.
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    ///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    /// The `name` field has been ommited in this struct's definition.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    pub len: u32,
[597](https://docs.rs#597)}
[598](https://docs.rs#598)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)
[600](https://docs.rs#600)extern {
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    /// Creates an inotify instance
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    ///
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// If you need more flexibility, consider using [`inotify_init1`] instead.
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// Returns `-1`, if an error occured, or an inotify file descriptor
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// otherwise.
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// Please refer to the [man page] for additional details.
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    ///
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// [`inotify_init1`]: fn.inotify_init1.html
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// [man page]: http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/inotify_init.2.html
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    pub fn inotify_init() -> c_int;
[613](https://docs.rs#613)
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// Creates an inotify instance
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    ///
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// Takes an argument to configure the new inotify instance. The following
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// flags can be set:
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    ///
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    /// - [`IN_CLOEXEC`]
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// - [`IN_NONBLOCK`]
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    ///
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    /// Returns `-1`, if an error occured, or an inotify file descriptor
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// otherwise.
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// Please refer to the [man page] for additional details.
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    ///
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// [`IN_CLOEXEC`]: constant.IN_CLOEXEC.html
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// [`IN_NONBLOCK`]: constant.IN_NONBLOCK.html
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// [man page]: http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/inotify_init1.2.html

Adds or updates an inotify watch

Adds an item to the watch list of an inotify instance, or modifies an item on that list. This function takes the following arguments:

- `fd`is the file descriptor of the inotify instance (created by- `inotify_init`- `inotify_init1`
- `pathname`is the path of the file or directory watch
- `mask`defines the behavior of this function and configures the watch

The following flags in `mask` control the type of events to watch for:

- `IN_ACCESS`
- `IN_ATTRIB`
- `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`
- `IN_CLOSE_WRITE`
- `IN_CREATE`
- `IN_DELETE`
- `IN_DELETE_SELF`
- `IN_MODIFY`
- `IN_MOVED_FROM`
- `IN_MOVED_TO`
- `IN_MOVE_SELF`
- `IN_OPEN`

The following constants can be used as shortcuts to set multiple event flags:

In addition, the following flags can be set to control the behaviors of the watch and this function:

The function returns `-1` if an error occured. Otherwise, it returns a
watch descriptor that can be used to remove the watch using
[ inotify_rm_watch](https://docs.rs/fn.inotify_rm_watch.html) or identify the watch via

[’s [wd`] field.](https://docs.rs/struct.inotify_event.html)

`inotify_event`Please refer to the [man page](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/inotify_add_watch.2.html) for additional details.

## Expand description

Removes an inotify watch

Returns `0` on success, `-1` on failure.

# inotify_event in inotify_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/inotify-sys/0.1.7/inotify_sys/struct.inotify_event.html

## Expand description

Describes a file system event

From [inotify(7)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html):

To determine what events have occurred, an application

[read(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/read.2.html)s from the inotify file descriptor. If no events have so far occurred, then, assuming a blocking file descriptor,[read(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/read.2.html)will block until at least one event occurs (unless interrupted by a signal, in which case the call fails with the error EINTR; see[signal(7)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal.7.html)).Each successful

[read(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/read.2.html)returns a buffer containing one or more of this structure.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.wd)

`wd: `[c_int](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/primitives/type.c_int.html)Identifies the watch for which this event occurs

This is one of the watch descriptors returned by a previous call to
[ inotify_add_watch()](https://docs.rs/fn.inotify_add_watch.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.mask)

`mask: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Describes the type file system event

One of the following bits will be set, to identify the type of event:

- `IN_ACCESS`
- `IN_ATTRIB`
- `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`
- `IN_CLOSE_WRITE`
- `IN_CREATE`
- `IN_DELETE`
- `IN_DELETE_SELF`
- `IN_IGNORED`
- `IN_MODIFY`
- `IN_MOVED_FROM`
- `IN_MOVED_TO`
- `IN_MOVE_SELF`
- `IN_OPEN`
- `IN_Q_OVERFLOW`
- `IN_UNMOUNT`

Some constants cover multiple bits, and can be used for a less precise check of the event type:

In addition, the [ IN_ISDIR](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_ISDIR.html) bit can be set.

A number that connects related events

Currently used only for rename events. A related pair of
[ IN_MOVED_FROM](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_MOVED_FROM.html) and

[events will have the same, non-zero, cookie. For all other events, cookie is 0.](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_MOVED_TO.html)

`IN_MOVED_TO`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.len)

`len: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The length of `name`

Used to determine the size of this structure. When `name`
isn’t present (`name` is only present when an event occurs
for a file inside a watched directory), it is 0. When `name`
*is* present, it counts all of `name`’s bytes, including `\0`.

The

`name`field is present only when an event is returned for a file inside a watched directory; it identifies the file pathname relative to the watched directory. This pathname is null-terminated, and may include further null bytes (‘\0’) to align subsequent reads to a suitable address boundary.

The `name` field has been ommited in this struct’s definition.

# IN_CLOEXEC in inotify_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/inotify-sys/0.1.7/inotify_sys/constant.IN_CLOEXEC.html

`pub const IN_CLOEXEC: `[c_int](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/primitives/type.c_int.html) = libc::O_CLOEXEC; // 524_288i32## Expand description

Set the `FD_CLOEXEC` flag for an inotify instance

Can be passed to [ inotify_init1](https://docs.rs/fn.inotify_init1.html) to set the

`FD_CLOEXEC` flag for the
inotify instance. This changes the behavior of file descriptor when
[execve(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html)’d. From

[fcntl(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fcntl.2.html):

If the FD_CLOEXEC bit is 0, the file descriptor will remain open across an

[execve(2)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html), otherwise it will be closed.

# inotify_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/inotify-sys/latest/inotify_sys/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#inotify-bindings-for-the-rust-programming-language)inotify bindings for the Rust programming language

Please note that these are direct, low-level bindings to C functions that
form the inotify C API. Unless you have a specific reason to use this crate,
[inotify-rs](https://crates.io/crates/inotify), which is an idiomatic wrapper, is a much better choice.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In general, inotify usage follows the following pattern:

- Create an inotify instance using `inotify_init``inotify_init1`
- Manage watches with `inotify_add_watch``inotify_rm_watch`
- Read event using `read`
- Close the inotify instance using `close`

Please refer to the [inotify man page](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html) and the rest of this documentation
for full details.

# libc 0.2.186 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libc/^0.2

# libc - Raw FFI bindings to platforms' system libraries

`libc` provides all of the definitions necessary to easily interoperate with C
code (or "C-like" code) on each of the platforms that Rust supports. This
includes type definitions (e.g. `c_int`), constants (e.g. `EINVAL`) as well as
function headers (e.g. `malloc`).

This crate exports all underlying platform types, functions, and constants under
the crate root, so all items are accessible as `libc::foo`. The types and values
of all the exported APIs match the platform that libc is compiled for.

Windows API bindings are not included in this crate. If you are looking for
WinAPI bindings, consider using crates like [windows-sys](https://docs.rs/windows-sys).

More detailed information about the design of this library can be found in its
[associated RFC](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/HEAD/text/1291-promote-libc.md).

## v1.0 Roadmap

Currently, `libc` has two active branches: `main` for the upcoming v1.0 release,
and `libc-0.2` for the currently published version. By default all pull requests
should target `main`; once reviewed, they can be cherry picked to the `libc-0.2`
branch if needed.

We will stop making new v0.2 releases once v1.0 is released.

See the section in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md#v10-roadmap) for more
details.

## Usage

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Features

-
`std`: by default`libc`links to the standard library. Disable this feature to remove this dependency and be able to use`libc`in`#![no_std]`crates.
-
`extra_traits`: all`struct`s implemented in`libc`are`Copy`and`Clone`. This feature derives`Debug`,`Eq`,`Hash`, and`PartialEq`.

The following features are deprecated:

- `use_std`: this is equivalent to- `std`
- `const-extern-fn`: this is now enabled by default
- `align`: this is now enabled by default

## Rust version support

The minimum supported Rust toolchain version is currently **Rust 1.65**.

Increases to the MSRV are allowed to change without a major (i.e. semver- breaking) release in order to avoid a ripple effect in the ecosystem. A policy for when this may change is a work in progress.

`libc` may continue to compile with Rust versions older than the current MSRV
but this is not guaranteed.

## Platform support

You can see the platform(target)-specific docs on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/libc), select a platform
you want to see.

See [ ci/verify-build.py](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/ci/verify-build.py) for
the platforms on which

`libc` is guaranteed to build for each Rust toolchain.
The test matrices at [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/actions)show the platforms in which

`libc` tests
are run.## License

at your option.

# inotify-sys 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/inotify-sys/0.1.0

Bindings for inotify

There are four types of statics:

- **Flags**, to be passed to- `inotify_init1()`
- **Events**, that describe which events should be watched for (when calling- `inotify_add_watch()`- `read()`
- **Options**, which can be added to the bit mask passed to- `inotify_add_watch()`
- **Infos**, indicating further details of the event that occured (returned by- `read()`

When events occur for monitored files and directories, those events
are made available to the application as structured data that can
be read from the inotify file descriptor using [ read()](https://docs.rs/libc/fn.read.html).

When all file descriptors referring to an inotify instance have been
closed (using [ close()](https://docs.rs/libc/fn.close.html)), the underlying object and its resources
are freed for reuse by the kernel; all associated watches are
automatically freed.

A programmer wanting to use inotify should also carefully read through
the [inotify(7)](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html) man page, which contains many caveats, warnings, and
recommendations for proper, robust, and efficient usage of inotify.

---

# inotify_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/inotify-sys

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#inotify-bindings-for-the-rust-programming-language)inotify bindings for the Rust programming language

Please note that these are direct, low-level bindings to C functions that
form the inotify C API. Unless you have a specific reason to use this crate,
[inotify-rs](https://crates.io/crates/inotify), which is an idiomatic wrapper, is a much better choice.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In general, inotify usage follows the following pattern:

- Create an inotify instance using `inotify_init``inotify_init1`
- Manage watches with `inotify_add_watch``inotify_rm_watch`
- Read event using `read`
- Close the inotify instance using `close`

Please refer to the [inotify man page](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html) and the rest of this documentation
for full details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [inotify_](https://docs.rs/struct.inotify_event.html)- event
- Describes a file system event

- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_ACCESS.html)- ACCESS

- Event: Any event occured

- Event: Metadata was changed

- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_CLOSE.html)- CLOSE

- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE.html)- CLOSE_ - NOWRITE
- Event: Non-writable file or directory was closed
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_CLOSE_WRITE.html)- CLOSE_ - WRITE
- Event: Writable file was closed
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_CREATE.html)- CREATE
- Event: File or directory was created in watched directory
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_DELETE.html)- DELETE
- Event: File or directory in watched directory was deleted
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_DELETE_SELF.html)- DELETE_ - SELF
- Event: Watched file or directory was deleted
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_DONT_FOLLOW.html)- DONT_ - FOLLOW
- Don’t dereference path, if it is a symbolic link
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_EXCL_UNLINK.html)- EXCL_ - UNLINK
- Ignore events for children, that have been unlinked from watched directory

- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_MOVE_SELF.html)- MOVE_ - SELF

- Set an inotify instance to non-blocking mode
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_ONESHOT.html)- ONESHOT
- Remove watch after one event
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_ONLYDIR.html)- ONLYDIR

- [IN_OPEN](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_OPEN.html)
- Event: File or directory was opened
- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_Q_OVERFLOW.html)- Q_ - OVERFLOW

- [IN_](https://docs.rs/constant.IN_UNMOUNT.html)- UNMOUNT
- Indicates that file system containing a watched object has been unmounted

# inotify-sys 0.1.7 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/inotify-sys/latest/source/build.rs

fnmain(){// On BSD systems, inotify is historically provided by a userspace library
// (libinotify) rather than the kernel. Link against it when building for
// those targets.
//// FreeBSD 14.4+ ships in-kernel inotify with libc wrappers in libc.so.7;
// when the `freebsd-native` feature is enabled we skip linking libinotify
// and let the extern declarations resolve against libc directly.
let target_os =std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").unwrap();let freebsd_native =std::env::var("CARGO_FEATURE_FREEBSD_NATIVE").is_ok();let needs_libinotify =match target_os.as_str(){"freebsd"=>!freebsd_native,"netbsd"|"openbsd"=>true,_=>false,};if needs_libinotify {// Use pkg-config to find the library search path if available,
// otherwise fall back to /usr/local/lib (the conventional BSD prefix).
let lib_dir =std::process::Command::new("pkg-config").args(["--variable=libdir","libinotify"]).output().ok().filter(|o|o.status.success()).and_then(|o|String::from_utf8(o.stdout).ok()).map(|s|s.trim().to_owned()).unwrap_or_else(||"/usr/local/lib".to_owned());println!("cargo:rustc-link-search=native={lib_dir}");println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=inotify");}}

# libc 0.2.186 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libc/0.2.186

# libc - Raw FFI bindings to platforms' system libraries

`libc` provides all of the definitions necessary to easily interoperate with C
code (or "C-like" code) on each of the platforms that Rust supports. This
includes type definitions (e.g. `c_int`), constants (e.g. `EINVAL`) as well as
function headers (e.g. `malloc`).

This crate exports all underlying platform types, functions, and constants under
the crate root, so all items are accessible as `libc::foo`. The types and values
of all the exported APIs match the platform that libc is compiled for.

Windows API bindings are not included in this crate. If you are looking for
WinAPI bindings, consider using crates like [windows-sys](https://docs.rs/windows-sys).

More detailed information about the design of this library can be found in its
[associated RFC](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/HEAD/text/1291-promote-libc.md).

## v1.0 Roadmap

Currently, `libc` has two active branches: `main` for the upcoming v1.0 release,
and `libc-0.2` for the currently published version. By default all pull requests
should target `main`; once reviewed, they can be cherry picked to the `libc-0.2`
branch if needed.

We will stop making new v0.2 releases once v1.0 is released.

See the section in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md#v10-roadmap) for more
details.

## Usage

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Features

-
`std`: by default`libc`links to the standard library. Disable this feature to remove this dependency and be able to use`libc`in`#![no_std]`crates.
-
`extra_traits`: all`struct`s implemented in`libc`are`Copy`and`Clone`. This feature derives`Debug`,`Eq`,`Hash`, and`PartialEq`.

The following features are deprecated:

- `use_std`: this is equivalent to- `std`
- `const-extern-fn`: this is now enabled by default
- `align`: this is now enabled by default

## Rust version support

The minimum supported Rust toolchain version is currently **Rust 1.65**.

Increases to the MSRV are allowed to change without a major (i.e. semver- breaking) release in order to avoid a ripple effect in the ecosystem. A policy for when this may change is a work in progress.

`libc` may continue to compile with Rust versions older than the current MSRV
but this is not guaranteed.

## Platform support

You can see the platform(target)-specific docs on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/libc), select a platform
you want to see.

See [ ci/verify-build.py](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/ci/verify-build.py) for
the platforms on which

`libc` is guaranteed to build for each Rust toolchain.
The test matrices at [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/actions)show the platforms in which

`libc` tests
are run.## License

This project is licensed under either of

at your option.

## Contributing

We welcome all people who want to contribute. Please see the
[contributing instructions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information.

Contributions in any form (issues, pull requests, etc.) to this project must
adhere to Rust's [Code of Conduct](https://www.rust-lang.org/policies/code-of-conduct).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted
for inclusion in `libc` by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be
dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.
